title: Your brain is hiding a hole in your vision

lines.text: Right now, there's a hole in your vision.
And your brain is hiding it from you.
Every eye has a blind spot, where the optic nerve leaves the back of the eye.
There are no light sensors there. At all.
And it's not tiny. It's wide enough to swallow eleven full moons, side by side.
So why don't you see a black hole?
Your brain paints over it, using whatever is around it.
Try it. Close your left eye, and stare at the cross.
Now slowly bring your phone closer.
At one distance, the dot simply vanishes.
Octopuses don't have this flaw. Their eyes are wired the other way round.
Which makes you wonder what else your brain is hiding, right now.

sources.claim: Blind spot is the optic disc, where the optic nerve leaves the eye; it has no light-detecting cells
Blind spot is about 7.5 degrees high and 5.5 degrees wide, 12-15 degrees to the temple side
Full Moon is about 31 arcminutes (half a degree) wide, so 5.5 / 0.5 = 11 moons across
The brain fills in the blind spot from the surrounding field; it is not seen as a hole
Octopus and squid photoreceptors face the light with nerves behind the retina, so they have no blind spot
Test works at about 3 to 3.7 times the cross-to-dot distance (about 16 to 20 cm for 5.3 cm on a phone)
